newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Fotilla sails to dispute Japan's island claims.
newsitem.headline: Fotilla sails to dispute Japan's island claims.

text.p: More than 200 activists sailed in a protest flotilla from Taiwan on Sunday to dispute Japan's claim to an island chain in the East China Sea.

"The Diaoyu Islands are our territory," the activists shouted, beating loud drums and singing patriotic songs as they set out for what is nominally described as a "fishing competition" near the islands.

The flotilla of 16 pleasure boats carrying activists from Taiwan and the United States left the northern port of Shenao at 10.50 p.m. (1450 GMT) for the Diaoyu Archipelago, which is claimed by Taiwan, China, and Japan.
They expected to take about eight hours to reach the islands, which lie 200 km (125 miles) north-east of Taiwan and are known in Japanese as the Senkaku Islands.
Some 20 activists from Hong Kong were to link up with the flotilla off Taiwan's coast.
Tokyo has stepped up security around the Diaoyus to bar entry into surrounding waters, Taiwan's state Central News Agency reported. The activists said they would not rule out landing on the Diaoyus.
All vessels were flying flags of the United States and Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government, activists said.

"The Diaoyu Island World Cup Fishing Contest is held in our territorial waters, we will seek help from (Taiwan's) coast guards if Japan interferes with our activity," protest leader Ching Chia-shou told reporters.

The cluster of uninhabited islands has ignited fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse there in July 1996.
Japan took the islands as war booty after defeating imperial China in 1895. China and Taiwan say they should have been returned after Japan's defeat in World War Two.

Officials said boat owners could have their licences revoked in their vessels sail to the archipelago. Taiwan fishing boats are not allowed to transport passengers and pleasure boats are forbidden to sail beyond 24 nautical miles off Taiwan's shores -- far short of the disputed islands.
Hong Kong activist David Chan drowned last September when he jumped from a protest boat into stormy waters near the islands to press China's claim.
